directAnswer: To scan a document, place it on the scanner bed and use the scanning software on your computer or the printer's control panel to initiate the scan.
summary: Scanning a document involves using a scanner or multifunction printer and appropriate software to digitize the physical document.

sections.heading: Types of Scanners
sections.body: There are flatbed scanners, sheet-fed scanners, and all-in-one printers that can scan. Each type may have different features and scanning methods.

sections.heading: Common Scanning Software
sections.body: Most scanners come with proprietary software, but you can also use built-in options like Windows Fax and Scan or macOS Preview.

steps.title: Prepare the Scanner
steps.detail: Ensure the scanner is connected to your computer and powered on. Place the document face down on the scanner bed.

steps.title: Open Scanning Software
steps.detail: Launch the scanning software on your computer. For Windows, search for 'Windows Fax and Scan'; for macOS, open 'Preview' and select 'Import from Scanner'.

steps.title: Select Scan Settings
steps.detail: Choose your desired settings such as file format (PDF, JPEG), resolution, and color options.

steps.title: Initiate the Scan
steps.detail: Click the 'Scan' button in the software to start the scanning process. Once completed, save the scanned document to your desired location.

faqs.question: What file formats can I save my scanned document in?
faqs.answer: You can typically save scanned documents in formats like PDF, JPEG, or TIFF, depending on the software used.

faqs.question: Can I scan multiple pages at once?
faqs.answer: Yes, if you have a sheet-fed scanner or an all-in-one printer with an automatic document feeder (ADF), you can scan multiple pages in one go.

faqs.question: What should I do if my scanner is not recognized by my computer?
faqs.answer: Check the USB connection, ensure the scanner is powered on, and install any necessary drivers from the manufacturer's website.

caveats: Scanning quality may vary based on the scanner's resolution settings and the condition of the document being scanned.
